clue.text: Exercises right to lead enterprise, perhaps

indicators.note: the first two pieces go in front of the next, leading it in the answer

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
an enterprise is a bold undertaking, an adventure

explanation.surface: A fitness instructor suggests that working out may give you the right spirit for a business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lead' tells you PE and R come before ADVENTURE. The answer is an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic adverb meaning by chance or possibly.

clue.text: Boy before girl on one knee

indicators.note: one name goes before the other in the answer, reading downward

parts.note: Pat is a boy's name
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young man drops onto one knee in front of his girlfriend to propose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one' simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, the bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: In anger smashed compass

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and breaks a compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass and range both mean the scope or extent of something.

clue.text: Humiliating in end game assault

indicators.note: an assault is a violent attack, so the letters of the three words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A chess player suffers a crushing, embarrassing attack as the end game approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but it is part of the fodder: IN, END and GAME together give the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeaning conduct lowers someone's dignity, so it is degrading.

clue.text: Flier from Sheerness

indicators.note: the bird is taken out of the place name, its letters running inside it

explanation.surface: A bird or pilot sets off from the Kentish port of Sheerness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent. The printed count (9) is a misprint for (4).
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Set up board prepared for examination

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the word set taken as written
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An examiner arranges the desks ready for an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns SET into TES, which then sits above TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something testable can be checked or examined, so it is open to a test.

clue.text: Doctor got up about one and made haste

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the next piece
in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, read backwards

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A physician jumps out of bed at one in the morning and hurries off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses DR to RD, and 'about' puts ACE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of to race, to go at speed, so it means hurried.

clue.text: South from organ rising in tempo

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed 'South from organ rising in tempo (8)' has no definition for RESONATE; RATE around ESON (NOSE reversed) accounts for the letters but nothing defines the answer, so the clue appears cut short.
annotationWithheld.clue: South from organ rising in tempo

clue.text: Beg to interrupt the stake holder

indicators.note: one word breaking into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a stake is a bet, money wagered
to beg is to ask

explanation.surface: A gambler pleads to cut in on the man holding the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link. The surface's 'stake holder' is a gambling term, but 'holder' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket is a container for carrying or keeping things.

clue.text: Permanent homes for English people in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the shelters

parts.note: tents give temporary shelter, as at a campsite
men are people

explanation.surface: Campers living under canvas are offered proper housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. E and MEN go inside TENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenements are blocks of flats; in law a tenement is any permanent property held by a tenant.

clue.text: Church a haven for the Spanish disciple

indicators.note: a haven gives shelter, so the first pieces shelter the next one inside them

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A church offers refuge to a follower from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: EL sits inside CH and A, between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is a pupil of a Hindu guru, a devoted follower.

clue.text: Scope for wager to secure small return

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast, so the bet wraps around the reversed piece

parts.note: to lay is to bet, as in laying odds

indicators.note: returning means the word for small is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A gambler has room to place a bet that brings in a modest win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses WEE to EEW, and 'to secure' puts it inside LAY. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, freedom of action.

clue.text: Possibly a manual worker to engage

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
to book is to engage or reserve

explanation.surface: A labourer who works with his hands is taken on for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual worker' looks like one phrase but it splits: 'manual' is the definition, 'worker' starts the wordplay. 'Possibly a' leads in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook is a guide giving instructions, which is what a manual is.

clue.text: Clear account and leave

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone settles their bill and walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit is to declare a defendant not guilty, clearing them of a charge.

clue.text: Challenge in quiz

definitions.meaning: to challenge a decision is to dispute or doubt it
to quiz someone is to interrogate them

explanation.surface: A contestant disputes a point in a quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the verb: to dispute a claim, and to interrogate a person with inquiries.

clue.text: Obvious accommodation for elderly relative to occupy

indicators.note: occupying a home means living inside it, so the relative goes inside the flat

parts.note: a flat is accommodation, an apartment
gran, a grandmother, is an elderly relative

explanation.surface: It is clear that a granny flat is meant for an aged family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring or conspicuous, plain for all to see.

clue.text: Material used for repairing Army breeches?

definitions.text: Material used for repairing Army breeches?

parts.words: Material used for repairing Army breeches?
parts.note: breeches suggests trousers to be patched with cloth, but a gun's breech is meant, and the material is an explosive, not fabric

explanation.surface: A quartermaster looks for cloth to patch soldiers' trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeches are knee-length trousers; the breech is the rear end of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Guncotton is nitrocellulose, an explosive made by treating cotton with acids, used in munitions.

clue.text: Tramp finds lost love wandering in mist

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for mist

parts.note: mist is fog

indicators.note: letters that wander move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A vagrant discovers that the sweetheart he lost is roaming through the mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' jumbles LOST and O into OOTSL, and 'in' puts that inside FOG. 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To footslog is to trudge or march wearily, which is to tramp.

clue.text: Get too big for superior sprout

parts.note: over means above or superior to
to sprout is to grow

explanation.surface: A plant outgrows its better-placed neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that overgrow a space spread across it, becoming too large for it.

clue.text: Establish a position in the East

definitions.meaning: to find one's bearings or set something facing a direction
the countries of Asia, in old-fashioned usage

explanation.surface: A traveller gets her bearings somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient is to find one's bearings; the Orient is the old name for the countries of Asia.

clue.text: An objective listener to inspire esteem

parts.note: an end is an objective or aim
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A goal-driven person who listens well wins people's respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone well liked, winning affection.

clue.text: Creature depositing eggs on growing grass

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing means rising upward, so the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An insect lays its eggs on a blade of new grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' reverses REED to DEER. 'depositing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer, an animal.

clue.text: Convey thanks turning in eventually

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the phrase for eventually

parts.note: in time means eventually

indicators.note: turning means the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets round to expressing gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA reversed gives AT, which goes inside IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to make known or hint at, communicating something indirectly.

clue.text: Damp fog and nothing to be seen in it

indicators.note: the nought is placed so that it shows within the word for fog

parts.note: mist is fog
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: In thick fog there is nothing visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'it' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet.

clue.text: Console for star virtuoso

parts.note: Sol is the sun, our star
an ace is an expert, a virtuoso

explanation.surface: A gaming console is wanted for a celebrity champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Console' looks like a games machine, a noun, but it is a noun meaning comfort. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort in distress, which is consolation.

clue.text: Giving imitation brooch in silver casing

indicators.note: a casing goes round something, so the symbol surrounds the brooch

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pin is a brooch

explanation.surface: A fake brooch is set in a silver case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping means copying or mimicking.

clue.text: Top-heavy weapon causing damage

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for heavy, as in pencil grades
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: An unbalanced weapon can do damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is injury or damage.

clue.text: Strange Omani girl

indicators.note: strange letters are odd, out of their normal order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric young woman from Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, from the Bible.

clue.text: Not so sagacious as the rest, at any rate in North America

definitions.text: Not so sagacious as the rest
definitions.meaning: the least clever of a group, read as two words

definitions.text: at any rate in North America
definitions.meaning: an American adverb meaning at least

explanation.surface: Someone is the dimmest of the group, at least in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means of least wisdom; as one, it is the US informal adverb for at least.

clue.text: A strange game played by one in the theatre

indicators.note: something played with is toyed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd game is played by a theatre employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage manager runs the practical side of a theatre production.
